title: SemiAnalysis details Trainium3 microarchitecture and inference cost results
summary: SemiAnalysis published a Trainium3 deep dive arguing that AWS&\#x27;s ML-first design—where tiles are a first-class primitive rather than an addition to a GPU thread model—now has sufficiently mature software to compete on inference. Its UBenchX microbenchmarks report that Trainium&\#x27;s Descriptor Generation Engines allow peak HBM bandwidth utilization at small message sizes, which the authors say is not possible on Nvidia GPUs, and cover cycle-level SRAM, rack-scale, and attention latency. On InferenceX, the firm reports that Trainium3 PDS with vLLM delivers better performance per TCO than every accelerator except Nvidia Vera Rubin across the TCO-versus-p90-interactivity frontier, while Trainium3 and TPUs trade blows with or beat GB300 on token-generation TCO; the supplied excerpt gives no absolute benchmark figures.
